claim: Physcomitrella patens has five identified class VIII myosin genes, named myo8A through E.
source: Physcomitrella patens has five identified class VIII myosin genes, named myo8A through E.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the number and naming of myosin VIII genes in P. patens, supported by citation to Wu et al. (2011).

claim: A line in which all five myosin VIII genes were disrupted (Δmyo8ABCDE) was constructed by Wu et al. (2011).
source: Taking advantage of facile homologous recombination in this species, Wu et al. (2011) constructed a line in which all five genes were disrupted (Δmyo8ABCDE).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wu et al. (2011).

claim: Protonemata from the Δmyo8ABCDE line have multiple, unevenly distributed branches.
source: Protonemata from this line have multiple, unevenly distributed branches.
evidence: This is an observation of the phenotype of the myosin VIII null mutant.

claim: Cell plate placement at branch sites is often affected in Δmyo8ABCDE plants.
source: Upon further inspection, we found that cell plate placement at branch sites is often affected (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Cell plates are aberrantly positioned with respect to the filament axis in Δmyo8ABCDE plants.
source: Cell plates are aberrantly positioned with respect to the filament axis (Figure 1A, arrows).
evidence: This is supported by visual evidence in Figure 1A.

claim: More than 84% of wild-type apical cell plates are within 15° of the perpendicular plane.
source: In young wild-type plants, apical cells position their new cell plates perpendicular to the long axis of the cell: more than 84% of apical cell plates are within 15° of the perpendicular plane.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of cell plate angles in wild-type plants.

claim: In myosin VIII null plants, less than 35% of the apical cell plates are within 15° of the perpendicular axis.
source: In contrast in myosin VIII null plants, less than 35% of the apical cell plates are within 15° of the perpendicular axis and nearly 40% have cell plates with angles greater than 25°, some as high as 45° (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement shown in Figure 1B comparing mutant to wild-type.

claim: Nearly 40% of myosin VIII null apical cells have cell plates with angles greater than 25°.
source: In contrast in myosin VIII null plants, less than 35% of the apical cell plates are within 15° of the perpendicular axis and nearly 40% have cell plates with angles greater than 25°, some as high as 45° (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Expression of Myo8A-GFP results in plants with 63% of the apical cell plates within 15° of the perpendicular axis.
source: To test this, we measured cell plate positioning in young plants and found that expression of Myo8A-GFP results in plants with 63% of the apical cell plates within 15° of the perpendicular axis.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement demonstrating partial rescue.

claim: Cell plates with angles greater than 35° are never observed in the Myo8A-GFP expressing plants.
source: Importantly, cell plates with angles greater than 35° are never observed in the Myo8A-GFP expressing plants (Figure 1B), indicating that Myo8A-GFP partially restores cell plate positioning in the myosin VIII null plants.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Myo8A-GFP partially restores cell plate positioning in the myosin VIII null plants.
source: Importantly, cell plates with angles greater than 35° are never observed in the Myo8A-GFP expressing plants (Figure 1B), indicating that Myo8A-GFP partially restores cell plate positioning in the myosin VIII null plants.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Myo8A-GFP expression partially rescues protonemal branching defects in myosin VIII null plants.
source: Additionally, Myo8A-GFP expression partially rescues a number of other defects in myosin VIII null plants, including protonemal branching defects (Figure 1C), apical cell length (Figure 1D), and timing of gametophore formation (data not shown).
evidence: This is supported by visual evidence in Figure 1C.

claim: Myo8A-GFP expression partially rescues apical cell length defects in myosin VIII null plants.
source: Additionally, Myo8A-GFP expression partially rescues a number of other defects in myosin VIII null plants, including protonemal branching defects (Figure 1C), apical cell length (Figure 1D), and timing of gametophore formation (data not shown).
evidence: This is supported by measurements shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Myo8A-GFP is functional.
source: Taken together, our data indicate that Myo8A-GFP is functional.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments showing partial restoration of multiple phenotypes.

claim: Myo8A-GFP localizes diffusely and as small particles throughout the cytoplasm.
source: Myo8A-GFP localizes diffusely and as small particles throughout the cytoplasm (Figure 2A) as well as at the cell cortex (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Myo8A-GFP localizes at the cell cortex.
source: Myo8A-GFP localizes diffusely and as small particles throughout the cytoplasm (Figure 2A) as well as at the cell cortex (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In apical cells Myo8A-GFP particles are enriched at the cell tip.
source: In apical cells Myo8A-GFP particles are enriched at the cell tip (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Myo8A-GFP cortical particles appear to move along actin filaments.
source: Using variable angle epifluorescence microscopy (VAEM), we simultaneously imaged Myo8A-GFP and actin labeled with lifeact-mCherry. We observed that Myo8A-GFP cortical particles appear to move along actin filaments, consistent with actin-based motility (Figure 2B; Video 1).
evidence: This is based on simultaneous imaging of Myo8A-GFP and actin shown in Figure 2B and Video 1.

claim: Movement of Myo8A-GFP was observed in both directions along an actin cable.
source: Movement was observed in both directions along an actin cable (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Myo8A-GFP moves at 0.65 ± 0.57 µm/s.
source: We measured the velocity of the particles and found that Myo8A-GFP moves at 0.65 ± 0.57 µm/s (n = 249 particles from 7 cells, Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement shown in Figure 2E.

claim: In the presence of 25 µM latrunculin B, Myo8A-GFP still localizes to the cell cortex but no longer exhibits directed motility.
source: In the presence of 25 µM latrunculin B (LatB), which depolymerizes the actin cytoskeleton, Myo8A-GFP still localizes to the cell cortex but no longer exhibits directed motility (Figure 2D; Video 2), as expected for an active, actin-based molecular motor.
evidence: This is based on drug treatment experiments shown in Figure 2D and Video 2.

claim: Myo8A-GFP is an active, actin-based molecular motor.
source: In the presence of 25 µM latrunculin B (LatB), which depolymerizes the actin cytoskeleton, Myo8A-GFP still localizes to the cell cortex but no longer exhibits directed motility (Figure 2D; Video 2), as expected for an active, actin-based molecular motor.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of directed motility upon actin depolymerization.

claim: In branch forming cells, Myo8A-GFP accumulates prominently at the cell cortex at the neck region of the emerging bulge prior to prophase.
source: In branch forming cells, Myo8A-GFP accumulates prominently at the cell cortex at the neck region of the emerging bulge, and this accumulation happens prior to prophase (Figure 3 arrows; Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Video 3).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 3 and Video 3.

claim: Branch forming cells lack a preprophase band.
source: The tubulin images confirm that these cells lack a preprophase band.
evidence: This is confirmed by tubulin imaging.

claim: During branch cell mitosis, Myo8A-GFP appears on the spindle and phragmoplast.
source: During branch cell mitosis, Myo8A-GFP appears on the spindle and phragmoplast, and as the phragmoplast matures, Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the phragmoplast periphery.
evidence: This is a direct observation during live-cell imaging.

claim: As the phragmoplast matures, Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the phragmoplast periphery.
source: During branch cell mitosis, Myo8A-GFP appears on the spindle and phragmoplast, and as the phragmoplast matures, Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the phragmoplast periphery.
evidence: This is a direct observation during live-cell imaging.

claim: In the later stages of cytokinesis, there are two populations of Myo8A-GFP: an inner ring on the phragmoplast and an outer ring at the cell cortex.
source: In the later stages of cytokinesis, there are two populations of Myo8A-GFP: an inner ring on the phragmoplast (Figure 3, arrow heads; Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and an outer ring at the cell cortex (Figure 3, arrows; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 3.

claim: As the phragmoplast expands, the inner Myo8A-GFP ring eventually reaches the outer one.
source: As the phragmoplast expands, the inner Myo8A-GFP ring eventually reaches the outer one.
evidence: This is a direct observation during live-cell imaging.

claim: Myosin VIII plays a role in ensuring that the phragmoplast expands to the pre-determined cortical division site.
source: Together with an increased frequency of cell plate positioning defects in myosin VIII null plants, these data suggest that myosin VIII plays a role in ensuring that the phragmoplast expands to the pre-determined cortical division site.
evidence: This is inferred from the localization data and the phenotype of the null mutant.

claim: Moss myosin VIII proteins are ∼50% identical to tobacco and Arabidopsis myosin VIIIs.
source: Alignment of myosin VIII proteins from tobacco, Arabidopsis and moss, revealed that moss myosin VIII proteins are ∼50% identical to tobacco and Arabidopsis myosin VIIIs (Figure 4—source data 1, 2).
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The percent identity between tobacco and Arabidopsis myosin VIIIs (excluding closely related Myo8B and D) is 51–58%.
source: Except for the closely related tobacco and Arabidopsis Myo8B and D, the percent identity between the remaining four tobacco and Arabidopsis myosin VIIIs is 51–58% (Figure 4—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis.

claim: Myo8A-GFP localizes in tobacco to dynamic cortical particles.
source: We found that similar to the interphase localization described above for moss, Myo8A-GFP localizes in tobacco to dynamic cortical particles (Figure 4A; Video 4).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 4A and Video 4.

claim: In tobacco cells about to enter mitosis, cortical Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the presumptive position of the preprophase band.
source: In cells about to enter mitosis, cortical Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the presumptive position of the preprophase band (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 4B.

claim: As tobacco cells enter mitosis, cortical Myo8A-GFP tightens into a thin band and remains at the cortical division site.
source: As cells enter mitosis, cortical Myo8A-GFP tightens into a thin band and remains at the cortical division site.
evidence: This is a direct observation during live-cell imaging.

claim: In early cytokinesis in tobacco, Myo8A-GFP appears at the phragmoplast midzone.
source: In early cytokinesis, Myo8A-GFP appears also at the phragmoplast midzone (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 4C.

claim: As the phragmoplast expands in tobacco, the Myo8A-GFP at the phragmoplast midzone expands out eventually reaching the Myo8A-GFP at the cortical division site.
source: As the phragmoplast expands, the Myo8A-GFP at the phragmoplast midzone expands out eventually reaching the Myo8A-GFP at the cortical division site (Figure 4D; Video 5).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 4D and Video 5.

claim: Before nuclear envelope break down, a population of Myo8A-GFP localizes to cytoplasmic microtubules surrounding the nucleus.
source: Before nuclear envelope break down, we found a population of Myo8A-GFP that localizes to cytoplasmic microtubules surrounding the nucleus (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Myo8A-GFP remains localized along microtubules as the spindle is assembled.
source: Myo8A-GFP remains localized along microtubules as the spindle is assembled (Figure 5B; Video 6).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 5B and Video 6.

claim: During mitosis, Myo8A-GFP continues to associate with the mitotic spindle, enriched at the midzone and to some extent at the poles.
source: During mitosis, Myo8A-GFP continues to associate with the mitotic spindle (Figure 5C; Video 7), enriched at the midzone and to some extent at the poles.
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 5C and Video 7.

claim: Prior to anaphase, a small population of Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the cortex near the spindle midzone.
source: Prior to anaphase, a small population of Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the cortex near the spindle midzone (Figure 5C, arrows; Video 7).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 5C and Video 7.

claim: During anaphase, Myo8A-GFP concentrates at the midzone.
source: During anaphase, Myo8A-GFP concentrates at the midzone.
evidence: This is a direct observation during live-cell imaging.

claim: Initially Myo8A-GFP is found throughout the phragmoplast midzone.
source: Initially Myo8A-GFP is found throughout the phragmoplast midzone (Figure 5C—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 5C—figure supplement 1.

claim: As the phragmoplast matures, Myo8A-GFP accumulates on the leading edge of the phragmoplast, ultimately forming a ring.
source: As the phragmoplast matures, Myo8A-GFP accumulates on the leading edge of the phragmoplast, ultimately forming a ring (Figure 5C, Figure 5C—figure supplement 1; Video 7).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 5C and Video 7.

claim: In apical cells, Myo8A-GFP does accumulate at the cell cortex, but this accumulation occurs later and is significantly more dynamic compared to branching cells.
source: Interestingly in apical cells, Myo8A-GFP does accumulate at the cell cortex, but in contrast to branching cells, this accumulation occurs later and is significantly more dynamic.
evidence: This is a comparative observation between apical and branching cells.

claim: When Myo8A-GFP appears on the spindle, there is little to no accumulation of lifeact-mCherry.
source: To test whether actin is involved in recruiting Myo8A-GFP to the mitotic spindle, we first imaged Myo8A-GFP and lifeact-mCherry in dividing cells (Figure 6A; Video 8, top). When Myo8A-GFP appears on the spindle, there is little to no accumulation of lifeact-mCherry.
evidence: This is a direct observation from simultaneous imaging shown in Figure 6A and Video 8.

claim: During the transition from spindle to phragmoplast, Myo8A-GFP concentrates at the midzone and lifeact-mCherry fluorescence rises above background levels in the vicinity of the phragmoplast.
source: During the transition from spindle to phragmoplast, Myo8A-GFP concentrates at the midzone and lifeact-mCherry fluorescence rises above background levels in the vicinity of the phragmoplast.
evidence: This is a direct observation from simultaneous imaging.

claim: When Myo8A-GFP fluorescence tightens into a thin band on the phragmoplast leading edge, the lifeact-mCherry fluorescence accumulates significantly around the phragmoplast.
source: However, when Myo8A-GFP fluorescence tightens into a thin band on the phragmoplast leading edge, the lifeact-mCherry fluorescence accumulates significantly around the phragmoplast (Figure 6A; Video 8, top).
evidence: This is a direct observation from simultaneous imaging shown in Figure 6A and Video 8.

claim: Early localization of Myo8A-GFP to the mitotic spindle is independent of actin.
source: The timing of the appearance of actin suggests that early localization of Myo8A-GFP to the mitotic spindle is independent of actin. To test this, we imaged cells entering mitosis in the presence of 25 µM Latrunculin B, which depolymerizes the actin cytoskeleton (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). Strikingly, Myo8A-GFP still accumulates on the mitotic spindle.
evidence: This is demonstrated by drug treatment experiments shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Myo8A-GFP still accumulates on the mitotic spindle in the presence of latrunculin B.
source: To test this, we imaged cells entering mitosis in the presence of 25 µM Latrunculin B, which depolymerizes the actin cytoskeleton (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). Strikingly, Myo8A-GFP still accumulates on the mitotic spindle.
evidence: This is a direct observation from drug treatment experiments.

claim: Myo8A-GFP recruitment to the mitotic spindle and behavior during mitosis is apparently independent of actin.
source: Thus, Myo8A-GFP recruitment to the mitotic spindle and behavior during mitosis is apparently independent of actin.
evidence: This is inferred from the latrunculin B treatment experiments.

claim: The majority of untreated, wild-type phragmoplasts deposit membrane uniformly, appearing as smooth FM4-64 staining in the midzone (80% of wild type cells, n = 55).
source: The majority of untreated, wild-type phragmoplasts deposit membrane uniformly, appearing as smooth FM4-64 staining in the midzone (80% of wild type cells, n = 55; Figure 7A; Video 9,).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation shown in Figure 7A and Video 9.

claim: Most myosin VIII null dividing cells have non-uniform FM4-64 staining (70% of Δmyo8ABCDE cells, n = 79).
source: In contrast, most myosin VIII null dividing cells have non-uniform FM4-64 staining (70% of Δmyo8ABCDE cells, n = 79; Figure 7B; Video 10).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation shown in Figure 7B and Video 10.

claim: Treatment of wild type dividing cells with Latrunculin B results in cells with similar defects in cell plate assembly as those observed in the myosin VIII null cells (70% of wild type cells treated with LatB, n = 50).
source: Interestingly, treatment of wild type dividing cells with Latrunculin B results in cells with similar defects in cell plate assembly as those observed in the myosin VIII null cells (70% of wild type cells treated with LatB, n = 50; Figure 7C; Video 11), indicating that the observed changes in the assembling cell plate result from compromising actin and myosin.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from drug treatment experiments shown in Figure 7C and Video 11.

claim: The observed changes in the assembling cell plate result from compromising actin and myosin.
source: Interestingly, treatment of wild type dividing cells with Latrunculin B results in cells with similar defects in cell plate assembly as those observed in the myosin VIII null cells (70% of wild type cells treated with LatB, n = 50; Figure 7C; Video 11), indicating that the observed changes in the assembling cell plate result from compromising actin and myosin.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity of phenotypes between myosin VIII null and latrunculin B treatment.

claim: Myo8A-GFP localizes to the ends of peripheral phragmoplast microtubules.
source: However, we also observed that Myo8A-GFP localizes to the ends of peripheral phragmoplast microtubules (Figure 8A,B, arrows; Video 12) that initiate from the edge of the phragmoplast and are initially unattached to the phragmoplast midzone.
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 8A,B and Video 12.

claim: Peripheral phragmoplast microtubules initiate from the edge of the phragmoplast and are initially unattached to the phragmoplast midzone.
source: However, we also observed that Myo8A-GFP localizes to the ends of peripheral phragmoplast microtubules (Figure 8A,B, arrows; Video 12) that initiate from the edge of the phragmoplast and are initially unattached to the phragmoplast midzone.
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 8 and Video 12.

claim: Before the phragmoplast reaches the cell cortex, there were three times fewer peripheral microtubules in control cells as compared to cells treated with latrunculin B.
source: Before the phragmoplast reaches the cell cortex, we found that there were three times fewer peripheral microtubules in control cells as compared to cells treated with latrunculin B.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison between control and drug-treated cells.

claim: In control cells, only 20% of the peripheral microtubules were still present after 20 s (n = 4 cells).
source: To test this, we identified peripheral microtubules in control and latrunculin B treated cells and followed them for 20 s. We found in control cells that only 20% of the peripheral microtubules were still present after 20 s (n = 4 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from time-lapse imaging.

claim: In latrunculin B treated cells, 89% of peripheral microtubules were still present after 20 s (n = 4 cells).
source: In contrast, 89% of peripheral microtubules were still present after 20 s in latrunculin B treated cells (n = 4 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from time-lapse imaging.

claim: In the presence of actin, peripheral microtubules are swiftly integrated into the expanding phragmoplast.
source: Taken together these data indicate that in the presence of actin peripheral microtubules are swiftly integrated into the expanding phragmoplast, suggesting that actin filaments exist between the edge of the expanding phragmoplast, peripheral microtubules, and the cell cortex.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of peripheral microtubule dynamics in control vs. drug-treated cells.

claim: Actin filaments exist between the edge of the expanding phragmoplast, peripheral microtubules, and the cell cortex.
source: Taken together these data indicate that in the presence of actin peripheral microtubules are swiftly integrated into the expanding phragmoplast, suggesting that actin filaments exist between the edge of the expanding phragmoplast, peripheral microtubules, and the cell cortex.
evidence: This is inferred from the dynamics of peripheral microtubules and the effect of actin depolymerization.

claim: For2A-GFP is enriched on the phragmoplast as soon as it forms from the late spindle.
source: In support of this, we found that an actin nucleator, For2A-GFP (van Gisbergen et al., 2012), is enriched on the phragmoplast as soon as it forms from the late spindle (Figure 9A; Video 13).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 9A and Video 13.

claim: For2A-GFP remains on the edge of the phragmoplast throughout cytokinesis.
source: For2A-GFP remains on the edge of the phragmoplast throughout cytokinesis (Figure 9B; Video 14), suggesting that actin is actively polymerized on the phragmoplast edge.
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 9B and Video 14.

claim: Actin is actively polymerized on the phragmoplast edge.
source: For2A-GFP remains on the edge of the phragmoplast throughout cytokinesis (Figure 9B; Video 14), suggesting that actin is actively polymerized on the phragmoplast edge.
evidence: This is inferred from the localization of the actin nucleator For2A-GFP.

claim: Actin accumulates at the midzone once the phragmoplast forms.
source: To test this, we simultaneously imaged lifeact-mEGFP and mCherry-tubulin using a laser scanning confocal microscope. We confirmed that actin accumulates at the midzone once the phragmoplast forms.
evidence: This is a direct observation from simultaneous imaging.

claim: As the phragmoplast expands out from the center of the cell towards the cell cortex, actin filaments are present at the midzone and between the leading edge of the phragmoplast and the cell cortex.
source: As the phragmoplast expands out from the center of the cell towards the cell cortex, we discovered that actin filaments are present at the midzone and between the leading edge of the phragmoplast and the cell cortex (Figure 9C; Video 15).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 9C and Video 15.

claim: Peripheral phragmoplast microtubules intersect the actin filaments that span the distance between the phragmoplast leading edge and the cell cortex.
source: Moreover, peripheral phragmoplast microtubules intersect the actin filaments that span the distance between the phragmoplast leading edge and the cell cortex (Figure 9C, arrowhead).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Microtubules may interact with actin filaments bridging the cell cortex and the phragmoplast during the time that myosin VIII-mediated motility guides the phragmoplast.
source: Our data suggest that microtubules may interact with actin filaments bridging the cell cortex and the phragmoplast during the time that myosin VIII-mediated motility guides the phragmoplast.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of microtubule-actin intersections and myosin VIII localization.

claim: A population of myosin VIII localizes to microtubules and this population incorporates into the mitotic spindle upon spindle formation.
source: Based on our data, we propose the following model for myosin VIII function in phragmoplast guidance during division of a protonemal apical cell (Figure 10). A population of myosin VIII localizes to microtubules and this population incorporates into the mitotic spindle upon spindle formation.
evidence: This is part of a model proposed based on the data presented.

claim: In early mitosis, as microtubules are dynamically searching to make chromosomal attachments, Myo8A-GFP decorates the entire spindle.
source: In early mitosis, as microtubules are dynamically searching to make chromosomal attachments, Myo8A-GFP decorates the entire spindle (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 5B.

claim: At metaphase, Myo8A-GFP concentrates in the spindle midzone.
source: At metaphase, Myo8A-GFP concentrates in the spindle midzone and at anaphase an additional population of Myo8A-GFP dynamically concentrates at the cell cortex where the cell plate ultimately fuses with the parental cell wall.
evidence: This is a direct observation during live-cell imaging.

claim: At anaphase an additional population of Myo8A-GFP dynamically concentrates at the cell cortex where the cell plate ultimately fuses with the parental cell wall.
source: At metaphase, Myo8A-GFP concentrates in the spindle midzone and at anaphase an additional population of Myo8A-GFP dynamically concentrates at the cell cortex where the cell plate ultimately fuses with the parental cell wall.
evidence: This is a direct observation during live-cell imaging.

claim: Once the phragmoplast assembles, Myo8A-GFP forms a tight ring at the edge of the expanding phragmoplast.
source: Once the phragmoplast assembles, Myo8A-GFP forms a tight ring at the edge of the expanding phragmoplast (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 5.

claim: For2A localizes to the phragmoplast and polymerizes actin filaments between the leading edge of the phragmoplast and the cell cortex.
source: At this point, the class II formin, For2A, localizes to the phragmoplast (Figure 9B; van Gisbergen et al., 2012) and polymerizes actin filaments between the leading edge of the phragmoplast and the cell cortex (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is based on direct observations shown in Figure 9B and 9C, and cited work.

claim: The barbed ends of the actin filaments are anchored at the phragmoplast midzone and the pointed ends are in the cytoplasm.
source: Since For2A remains associated with the phragmoplast, it suggests that the barbed ends of the actin filaments are anchored at the phragmoplast midzone and the pointed ends are in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is inferred from the localization of For2A and knowledge of formin function.

claim: Myosin VIII at the cortex can hold onto actin filaments and walk towards the barbed end thereby aligning the actin filaments to the cortical division site.
source: Myosin VIII at the cortex can hold onto these actin filaments and walk towards the barbed end thereby aligning the actin filaments to the cortical division site.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on myosin VIII localization and motor activity.

claim: Myosin VIII at the ends of peripheral phragmoplast microtubules moves along actin filaments from the cortical division site towards the expanding phragmoplast, thereby translocating microtubules and ensuring that phragmoplast expansion occurs along a plane defined by the cortical division site.
source: We propose that myosin VIII at the ends of peripheral phragmoplast microtubules moves along these actin filaments from the cortical division site towards the expanding phragmoplast, thereby translocating microtubules and ensuring that phragmoplast expansion occurs along a plane defined by the cortical division site (Figure 10).
evidence: This is the proposed model based on all the data presented.

claim: In the budding yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the class V myosin, Myo2p, binds Kar9p, which localizes to cytoplasmic microtubule plus ends by binding the yeast EB1 homolog, Bim1p.
source: In the budding yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the class V myosin, Myo2p, binds Kar9p, which localizes to cytoplasmic microtubule plus ends by binding the yeast EB1 homolog, Bim1p (Beach et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Beach et al., 2000.

claim: Cytoplasmic microtubules in budding yeast emanate from the spindle pole body embedded in the nuclear envelope and Myo2p mediates their motility along actin cables directed into the bud, moving the nucleus toward the bud neck.
source: These cytoplasmic microtubules emanate from the spindle pole body embedded in the nuclear envelope and Myo2p mediates their motility along actin cables directed into the bud, moving the nucleus toward the bud neck (Beach et al., 2000; Yin et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Beach et al., 2000 and Yin et al., 2000.

claim: Myosin VIII in protonemata is mostly dispensable for phragmoplast guidance in apical cells.
source: While the localization of myosin VIII is striking, myosin VIII in protonemata is mostly dispensable for phragmoplast guidance in apical cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the mild phenotype in apical cells.

claim: Apical cells are narrow, with diameters not much greater than the sizes of the nucleus and spindle, leaving little room for those two structures to be misplaced.
source: These cells are narrow, with diameters not much greater than the sizes of the nucleus and spindle, leaving little room for those two structures to be misplaced.
evidence: This is a description of the geometry of apical cells.

claim: Due to geometric constraints in apical cells, the mitotic spindle always forms along the long axis of the cell.
source: Due to these geometric constraints, the mitotic spindle always forms along the long axis of the cell.
evidence: This is inferred from the geometry of apical cells.

claim: Any cell plate positioning defects that occur in apical cells are mild because the spindle midzone is always roughly perpendicular to the long axis of the cell.
source: Thus, any cell plate positioning defects that occur are mild because the spindle midzone is always roughly perpendicular to the long axis of the cell.
evidence: This is inferred from the geometry and spindle orientation.

claim: Myosin VIII is needed for branch formation, insofar as cell plates are often aberrantly positioned in the branching cells of the myosin VIII nulls.
source: In contrast, myosin VIII is needed for branch formation, insofar as cell plates are often aberrantly positioned in the branching cells of the myosin VIII nulls.
evidence: This is based on the observed phenotype in branching cells.

claim: In comparison to apical cell division, side-branch formation needs to specify the cell division plane more accurately.
source: Arguably, in comparison to apical cell division, side-branch formation needs to specify the cell division plane more accurately.
evidence: This is inferred from the geometry and requirements of branch formation.

claim: Branching involves an asymmetric cell division in an L-shaped cell.
source: Branching involves an asymmetric cell division in an L-shaped cell.
evidence: This is a description of the branching process.

claim: In branching cells, the nucleus migrates toward the junction of the parental cell and the branch and the spindle is oriented along the longitudinal axis of the new emerging cell.
source: The nucleus migrates toward the junction of the parental cell and the branch and the spindle is oriented along the longitudinal axis of the new emerging cell.
evidence: This is a description of the branching process.

claim: The phragmoplast builds the new cell plate at the junction of the two cells during branch formation.
source: The phragmoplast builds the new cell plate at the junction of the two cells.
evidence: This is a description of the branching process.

claim: In branching cells, a relatively static population of Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the cell cortex at the future site of cell division.
source: We found that in branching cells, a relatively static population of Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the cell cortex at the future site of cell division (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 3.

claim: In branching cells, Myo8A-GFP accumulates at the cortical site early, prior to mitosis, and remains throughout cytokinesis.
source: Myo8A-GFP accumulates at this site early, prior to mitosis, and remains throughout cytokinesis.
evidence: This is a direct observation during live-cell imaging.

claim: The new cell plate fuses with the parental cell membranes at the cortical site defined by the presence of Myo8A-GFP.
